Steady-state Kalman filter

Source: R/estimation.R
ctrl_kalman.Rd

For the model $$x_{k+1} = A x_k + B u_k + G w_k, \quad y_k = C x_k + D u_k + v_k$$ (or its continuous time analogue) with \(E[w w^\top] = Q_n\), \(E[v v^\top] = R_n\), \(E[w v^\top] = N_n\), compute the steady-state Kalman gains from the filtering Riccati equation (the dual of the LQR equation).

Usage

ctrl_kalman(sys, Qn, Rn, Nn = NULL, G = NULL)

Arguments

sys

A ctrl_ss model.

Qn

Process noise covariance (size ncol(G)).

Rn

Measurement noise covariance (p x p).

Nn

Optional cross covariance (ncol(G) x p).

G

Process noise input matrix; defaults to the identity (noise on every state).

Value

An object of class c("ctrl_kalman", "ctrl_estimator") with L, M (discrete only), P, Z (discrete only), poles (eigenvalues of \(A - L C\)), and system (the predictor as a ctrl_ss model with inputs u then y).

Details

Discrete time conventions: P is the steady-state prior covariance \(P_{k|k-1}\); M is the measurement-update (innovation) gain \(M = P C^\top (C P C^\top + R_n)^{-1}\) used in \(\hat x_{k|k} = \hat x_{k|k-1} + M (y_k - C\hat x_{k|k-1} - D u_k)\); L is the one-step predictor gain \(L = (A P C^\top + G N_n)(C P C^\top + R_n)^{-1}\) used in \(\hat x_{k+1|k} = A \hat x_{k|k-1} + B u_k + L(y_k - C \hat x_{k|k-1} - D u_k)\); Z is the posterior covariance \(P_{k|k}\) (for \(N_n = 0\)). In continuous time, L is the Kalman-Bucy gain \((P C^\top + G N_n) R_n^{-1}\).

Rn must be positive definite: perfect (noise-free) measurements make the filtering problem singular and are not silently regularized. Qn may be singular (including zero) as long as the Riccati equation has a stabilizing solution; this requires \((A, C)\) detectable and no unreachable noise modes on the stability boundary.

See also

ctrl_kalman_filter() for the time-varying filter.

Examples

sys <- ctrl_ss(matrix(c(1, 0.1, 0, 1), 2, byrow = TRUE), c(0.005, 0.1),
               c(1, 0), dt = 0.1)
kf <- ctrl_kalman(sys, Qn = diag(c(1e-4, 1e-3)), Rn = 0.01)
kf$M
#>           [,1]
#> [1,] 0.2372931
#> [2,] 0.2761715
